science.qualification: Photosphere color from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum, dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 computes from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 6,076 K (the record) and log g 4.32 (from the record's mass and radius (packages/astronomy/data/bodies/af-lep.json)): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. The disc is unresolved: no map or absolute brightness is implied. Self-luminous, so no lighting.

science.label: Dec 2007
science.description: Radial component of the star's large-scale magnetic field, fitted with ZDIpy to 19 ESPaDOnS spectra of 27 December 2007 to 30 December 2007 (reduced chi-square 1.30, against 1.9 with no field); mean field 20 G. A reduction made in this project, not a published map. Black line: 57 degrees south, below which the star never faces us.
science.title: ESPaDOnS · magnetic map made here · Dec 2007

science.label: Sector 32
science.description: Brightness of the star's surface that reproduces its light as it turns once in 1.01 days, fitted with starry to the light curve this project measured from the TESS full-frame images of sector 32 (the light swings by 1.7%; the map's curve leaves a scatter of 0.44%, the light's own noise being 0.09%). A light curve fixes how bright each longitude is, not the latitude of what darkens it. The map is made at the tilt the page draws the star with, 57°. Gaia DR3 lists 13 other stars within 63 arcseconds, giving under 0.1% of the light in the star's pixels. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · brightness map made here · Sector 32

science.label: Color + brightness
science.description: The star's color (#fdf5ff, its Color dataset) over the brightness map this project made from the star's light in TESS sector 32 (November and December 2020): the map's scale, 98% to 102% of the mean surface, runs from a darker, richer tone of the same hue to the color itself. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the parts can be told apart: the darkest part gives 3.7% less light than the brightest. Longitudes are fixed by the light curve; latitudes and shapes are not. No color change of the spots is drawn: none is measured. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · the star in its color over its brightness map · November and December 2020
